questions.topic_aspect: Basic circle vocabulary (radius, chord, tangent, diameter)
questions.correct_answer: (a) S is the tangent. (b) R is the chord (not a diameter).
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) B1 for identifying $S$ as the tangent (the line touching the circle at exactly one point, not crossing through the interior).
(b) B1 for identifying $R$ as the chord that is not a diameter (a line joining two points on the circumference that does not pass through the centre $O$) — accept reasoning that distinguishes it from $Q$ (the diameter, which passes through centre $O$) and $P$ (the radius, which only reaches from centre to circumference).
questions.misconception_targeted: Confusing chord with diameter, or tangent with radius

questions.topic_aspect: Angle in a semicircle is 90 degrees
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for recognising that angle PQR = 90 degrees (angle in a semicircle, since PR is a diameter)
A1 for x = 180 - 90 - 34 = 56 (using angle sum of triangle = 180 degrees)
questions.misconception_targeted: Not recognising diameter as the key trigger for 90 degree angle

questions.topic_aspect: Angle at centre is twice angle at circumference
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for recognising that the angle at the centre (136°) is twice the angle at the circumference, i.e. setting up x = 136 ÷ 2 (or equivalent correct method)
A1 for x = 68 (degrees), with correct units/notation

Note: award M0 if student doubles instead of halves (giving 272°, a misconception to be corrected) or applies the theorem to the reflex angle without justification.
questions.misconception_targeted: Halving instead of doubling, or applying theorem to non-corresponding arc

questions.topic_aspect: Angles in the same segment are equal
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for identifying that angles ACB and ADB are subtended by the same chord (AB) from the same side, so they are angles in the same segment.
A1 for x = 47 (degrees), with correct reasoning stated (e.g. "angles in the same segment are equal").
questions.misconception_targeted: Not recognising which angles subtend the same arc

questions.topic_aspect: Cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles sum to 180
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for using opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180 degrees: (3x+5) + (2x+15) = 180
M1 for correctly solving the resulting equation: 5x + 20 = 180, leading to x = 32... (working: 5x = 160, x = 32) -- accept correct rearrangement leading to a value of x
A1 for correct value of angle ABD = 3(31)+... [note: numbers chosen so 5x+20=180 gives x=32, so ABD = 3(32)+5 = 101] -- final answer 101 degrees, with no error in method; deduct if adjacent angles (ABD and BDC as if adjacent, summing to 360) were used instead of the correct opposite-angle relationship (misconception: adding adjacent angles instead of using opposite angles = 180)
questions.misconception_targeted: Adding adjacent angles instead of opposite angles

questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for recognising angle OTP = 90 degrees (tangent perpendicular to radius)
M1 for using angle sum of triangle OTP: angle TOP = 180 - 90 - 34
A1 for x = 56 (cao)
questions.misconception_targeted: Forgetting tangent meets radius at exactly 90 degrees

questions.topic_aspect: Two tangents from an external point are equal length
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for using the tangent-radius right angle to state angle OAP = angle OBP = 90 degrees
M1 for using angle sum of quadrilateral OAPB (or triangle properties): 360 - 90 - 90 - 34 = 146, then dividing by 2 (since OA = OB gives isosceles triangle OAP, OBP equal), or equivalently using triangle OAP: angle AOP = (180 - 34)/2 approach adapted correctly
A1 for x = 73 (degrees), with correct reasoning that tangents from an external point are equal in length, forming two congruent right-angled triangles, so angle PAO = (180 - 34)/2 = 73
questions.misconception_targeted: Assuming tangent lengths differ or forgetting isosceles triangle formed

questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for identifying that the angle between tangent $PT$ and chord $AC$ (i.e. angle $CAT = 71^\circ$) is equal to the angle in the alternate segment, which is the angle subtended by $AC$ at the circumference on the opposite side of the chord — this is angle $ABC$ (i.e. angle $x$).
M1 for correctly applying the alternate segment theorem: angle in alternate segment = angle between tangent and chord.
A1 for $x = 71^\circ$, with correct reasoning stated (e.g. "angle in alternate segment equals angle between tangent and chord").

Note: award 0 for M1 if student instead equates $71^\circ$ to angle $ACB$ or angle $BAC$ (matching to wrong segment).

5x + 95 = 180
5x = 85

(2x+10)+(3x+5)+90=180

questions.topic_aspect: Alternate segment theorem applied to a tangent laser beam on a circular telescope mirror, combined with triangle angle sum, requiring correct identification of tangent point and relevant chord
questions.correct_answer: (a) angle BCA = 34 degrees (b) angle CBA = 64 degrees
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for correctly applying the alternate segment theorem: identifying that the angle between tangent TCM and chord CA (angle ACT, in the alternate segment to angle CBA... — specifically recognising angle MCB = angle CAB is NOT the pair used here; instead using angle between tangent and chord CA equals angle in alternate segment CBA) — award M1 for identifying angle TCA = angle CBA OR equivalent correct alternate segment pairing leading to a valid equation using the triangle ABC angle sum: angle BCA = 180 - 82 - angle ABC, combined with tangent-chord angle MCB = 64 degrees = angle BAC in alternate segment (used as a check), then angle BCA found via triangle angle sum once angle ABC is found in part (b) is not required first; accept the direct route: 
M1 for using triangle angle sum in triangle $ABC$: angle $BCA$ = 180 - angle $BAC$ - angle $ABC$ where angle $ABC$ is found independently, OR M1 for correctly stating angle $BCA$ = 180 - 82 - 64 = 34 (using angle CBA = 64 from alternate segment theorem applied in part (b) reasoning, accepted if shown clearly with correct logic order)
A1 for angle BCA = $34^\circ$ (with correct supporting reasoning)

(b) M1 for correctly applying the alternate segment theorem: angle between tangent $MC$ and chord $CB$ (=64 degrees) equals the angle in the alternate segment, angle $CAB$ (already given as 82, so this pairing must instead be angle between tangent and chord $CB$ equals angle $CAB$ is NOT consistent -- correct pairing: angle $MCB$ = angle $BAC$ only if $BAC$ subtends $CB$; instead correctly angle $MCB$ = angle $CAB$ is the standard alternate segment result, so angle $CBA$ is instead found via triangle angle sum) 
A1 for angle $CBA$ = 180 - 82 - 34 = $64^\circ$

(Accept fully correct alternative valid methods using the alternate segment theorem and triangle angle sum reaching the same final answers, with correct geometric justification at each step.)
questions.misconception_targeted: Misidentifying tangent point and chord in applied context

questions.topic_aspect: Multi-step problem combining tangent-radius property, angle sum in triangle, and cyclic quadrilateral angle rule
questions.correct_answer: (a) Angle OAT = 90 degrees (tangent is perpendicular to radius). (b) Angle AOB = 56 degrees. (c) Angle ABC = 62 degrees.
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) B1 for angle OAT = 90 degrees, with reason "tangent is perpendicular to radius" (angle between tangent and radius is 90 degrees).

(b) Triangle OAT: angles sum to 180 degrees, so angle AOT = 180 - 90 - 34 = 56 degrees.
M1 for using angle sum of triangle OAT = 180 degrees (90 + 34 + angle AOT = 180)
A1 for angle AOB = angle AOT = 56 degrees (since O, B, T lie on the same straight line, angle AOB is the same as angle AOT)

(c) Cyclic quadrilateral ABCD: opposite angles sum to 180 degrees.
Angle ABC + angle ADC = 180 degrees
Angle ABC = 180 - 118 = 62 degrees
M1 (implied within final calculation) for using cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles sum to 180 degrees
A1 for angle ABC = 62 degrees

(Note: part (b) answer of 56 degrees is not required for part (c), testing whether students correctly select cyclic quadrilateral rule rather than incorrectly combining with earlier tangent/triangle results.)
questions.misconception_targeted: Losing track of which rule to apply at each stage in multi-step reasoning

questions.topic_aspect: Show that — combining angle at centre and alternate segment theorem
questions.correct_answer: x = 15, giving angle BCT = angle ABC = 40 degrees
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for using the angle at centre theorem to write angle ABC = (1/2)(4x+10) = (2x+5)° [angle at centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc AC]
M1 for using the alternate segment theorem to state angle BCT = angle BAC is NOT directly what's needed; correct reasoning: angle ABC (in the alternate segment to angle BCT) must equal angle BCT by the alternate segment theorem, so set up the equation (2x+5) = (3x-5)
M1 for solving the equation: 2x + 5 = 3x - 5 leading to x = 10... 

[Corrected working shown below for clarity of mark allocation]

M1: angle ABC = 1/2 × (4x+10) = (2x+5)° (angle at centre = twice angle at circumference on same arc)
M1: By alternate segment theorem, angle BCT = angle BAC is not used; instead angle ABC = angle BCT (angle in alternate segment equals angle between tangent and chord)
M1: Forms and solves equation (2x+5) = (3x-5) ⟹ x = 10 is INCORRECT — recompute: 2x+5=3x-5 ⟹ 10=x, so x=10, giving angle ABC = 25°, angle BCT = 25°.
A1: States correctly x = 10, with both angles equal to 25°, and concludes equality confirmed only when x = 10, verified by substitution.
questions.misconception_targeted: Failing to link two separate theorems into one coherent proof chain
